newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU ministers fail to cut deal on leg-hold traps.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers fail to cut deal on leg-hold traps.

text.p: Four EU countries on Thursday blocked a draft deal on international standards for leg-hold traps used to catch furred animals, throwing open a file which has divided the EU, Canada, Russia and the United States.
"The presidency withdrew the item from the agenda," an EU diplomat said after the Netherlands, the current president, failed to win backing for the draft trap standards.
The outcome is likely to sour Friday's planned EU/Canada bilateral meeting, due to take place in the margins of the Group of Seven industrialised nations summit in Denver, United States.
Austria, Belgium, Britain and France rejected the plan, together packing sufficient voting weight to stop a deal which Britain, for one, has said does little to stop animal suffering.
The result delighted Stanley Johnson, European affairs director of the International Fund for Animal Welfare, and other animal welfare lobbyists watching the Luxembourg meeting.
"For the fourth time, the Council of Ministers has rejected the European Commission's proposal for a so-called international humane trapping standard," Johnson said.

He said the EU executive should now go ahead and introduce a ban on fur imports from countries using leg-hold traps, a ban which has been on ice since January 1, 1996, as trap norms talks continued between the Commission, Canada and Russia.
But Canadian official Jim Stone expressed despair.
"Europe cannot make a decision... It's not good news," said Stone, first secretary to Canada's EU mission in Brussels.
"We have negotiated in good faith, this is a good agreement. We cannot understand why it's being turned down," he said.
Canada has fought hard to secure trap standards in place of a fur ban which it says would hit its aboriginal trapping communities hard.
